description: Produce a lightweight structural outline of a source file using a line-oriented scan (no full parser). Input supplies a file name, a language label, and the raw source text. The first output line is a file header reporting the file's base name, its language label, and its total line count. Each subsequent line describes one detected top-level construct in source order: its kind (function, class, struct, trait, impl, interface, type), an extracted name, and its 1-based line number. Constructs are recognised by keyword patterns appearing on a line (e.g. 'fn', 'struct', 'impl', 'trait', 'mod'/'def'/'func'/'class'/'function'/'async'); the name is the token following the recognised keyword with trailing punctuation stripped. At most thirty constructs are reported.

cases.expected_output:
file=test.rs language=rust lines=32
struct	TestStruct	2
impl	TestStruct	7
function	new	8
function	test_method(&self	15
function	test_function	20
trait	TestTrait	24
function	trait_method(&self	25
function	module_function	29
